answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because violet only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, kernel is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Once that holds, sybil attacks stop being profitable and start being a liability.
